Morgan (Finance): Heads-up — Finance needs a concise proposal for Q3 spot chargebacks. Wanted to float a concept: bucketed safety layers + a small per-job 'spot tax' to stabilize chargebacks across teams. Thoughts?
Sam (Eng-Infra): I can put together the numbers. remind me — target metric is per-GPU-hour effective cost including interruption tail, right?
Morgan (Finance): Yep. We want: 1) expected unit saving vs on-demand, 2) variance (stddev), 3) tail-risk buffer estimate (95th pct), and 4) a recommended spot-tax % to allocate to a central buffer. Keep it per-job and per-team.
Priya (FinOps): Example calc for a job:
```
on_demand = $3.00/hour
spot_discount = 0.68  # i.e. average spot saves 68%
interrupt_rate = 0.07  # prob of eviction during long jobs
interruption_penalty = $2.50  # extra cost + re-run + delays
effective_spot_cost = on_demand*(1-spot_discount) + interrupt_rate*interruption_penalty
```
That gives a baseline we can roll up.
Sam (Eng-Infra): Quick ballpark with our current aggregates: avg spot saving 68%, stddev ~9%, mean interruption rate ~6.5% (varies by zone). Using Priya's numbers: effective_spot_cost ~= $3*(0.32)+0.065*2.5 = $0.96+0.1625 = $1.1225/hr. So ~62% saving vs on-demand after accounting for interruptions.
cost-bot: snapshot: region-agg: us-west2 saving=70% sd=8.2% | us-east1 saving=66% sd=9.7% | eu-central saving=64% sd=10.1% | global avg=68% sd=9.0% | last_update=1766120000
Diego (Eng-SRE): Two operational notes: 1) Interruption penalty isn't just $$ — it's also latency and SLA risk. For low-latency endpoints we'll keep on-demand/reserved. 2) For batch jobs, fallback to another pool adds network & transfer delays. That should be modeled.
Lena (Product): If we add a per-job spot tax, how will teams perceive it? Would it show up as a line item in the console? We need a simple UX story.
Priya (FinOps): Proposal: bucketed safety layers = 3 buckets per region: 
- Bucket A (critical): on-demand / reserved only
- Bucket B (preferred spot): jobs with checkpointing & short windows; lower tax
- Bucket C (best-effort): long batch, retry-friendly; higher tax but biggest savings
Spot-tax formula (draft):
spot_tax_pct = base_tax + variance_surcharge
where base_tax = 4% (operations overhead) and variance_surcharge = min(8%, k * region_stddev)
k tuned so eu regions with 10% sd pay ~8% surcharge.
Sam (Eng-Infra): Implementation-wise we can compute per-region rolling stats and tag job runs with the tax at chargeback time. We already emit job metadata (region, duration, preemptible=true). Would need small billing pipeline change.
Morgan (Finance): Can you sketch numbers for one region (us-east1) and one team (ml-research) with historical run mix? We need: current billed spend, projected savings, recommended tax, and buffer contribution.
Sam (Eng-Infra): I have a quick calc for ml-research last 30d:
- on_demand_equiv_hours: 12,400h
- raw_spot_hours: 9,300h
- avg_spot_price = $0.96/hr (across shapes)
- implied on_demand_rate = $3.00/hr
Raw savings = (3.0 - 0.96)*9300 = $18,684
Accounting for interruptions & tail buffer reduces realized savings by ~15% -> realized savings ≈ $15.9k
If we set base_tax 4% + variance_surcharge 6% = 10% tax on realized savings => contribution to central buffer ~ $1.59k for the period.
Diego (Eng-SRE): Agree with the buffer allocation. We should earmark buffer for: immediate re-run credits (40%), cross-region failover costs (30%), and a small continuity fund for reserved fallback (30%).
Lena (Product): UX: show 'Spot Buffer' in billing with breakdown: tax %, buffer balance, and recent payouts. Keep it optional on onboarding but default on. :+1:
Priya (FinOps): Monte Carlo note: we'll run 10k sims per region varying: spot_discount ~ N(mu=0.68, sd=0.09), interrupt_rate ~ Beta(α=2, β=30) to capture heavy tail. Output: median saving, 90/95pct downside.
Sam (Eng-Infra): I'll start the run and attach a small sample output. Quick sample (toy):
```
region: us-east1
sim_median_saving = 62%
sim_95pct_downside = 42%
required_buffer_pct_for_95 = 12%
```
Morgan (Finance): That 12% figure is the kind of thing execs will want. If buffer needed ~12% of saved spend, we should compare to proposed tax (10% in Sam's example). Either raise tax or cap payouts.
Diego (Eng-SRE): Ops ask: also compute buffer draw frequency (how often buffer would be used to cover re-runs) — that impacts runway.
Priya (FinOps): Agreed. We'll also show two policy options: conservative (tax=12%) and lean (tax=8% + quarterly review).
Sam (Eng-Infra): Action items: 1) I'll run full Monte Carlo per region + per-team slices and put CSVs in /reports/finops/ by Fri EOD. 2) Small billing change PR to apply spot_tax tag for chargeback.
Morgan (Finance): Perfect. Please cc me and Priya when results land. Thanks all.
Lena (Product): Thanks — happy to help with the UI copy and console row.
